Shri Arvind Singh-Government Advocate for the respondent

Heard on IA No. 20114/2022, an application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant No.2-Rakesh Kol arising out of judgment dated 28.09.2022 delivered in ST. No.4100959/2020 by learned Additional Sessions Judge,
Sirmour District-Rewa.
T h e appellant has been convicted under Section 304B of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.1000/-, under Section 498A of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 1 year with fine of Rs.500/- and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 1 year with fine of Rs.500/- with default stipulations.

Learned counsel for the appellant after referring to prosecution evidence specially PW-1, PW-2,
PW-3 submits that from evidence on record, no demand of dowry and harassment with respect thereto is proved.
From evidence on record, it is also not proved that deceased committed suicide on account of demand of dowry and harassment.
It is also established from oral evidence that appellant is residing separately from his brother and deceased and he is the brother-in-law of deceased.
As per medical evidence, no injury has been found on the person of deceased.
The deceased committed suicide on account of being asked to do work in village.
Therefore, the jail sentence of appellant -Rakesh Kol may be suspended.
The prayer is opposed by learned counsel for the State.
In view of testimonies of PW-1, PW-2, PW-3 and PW-10, I deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant.

Subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant- Rakesh Kol is hereby suspended and it is directed that the he be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees thirty thousand only) with one solvent Narendra Kol vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69319524/
